Hi,
I think the only problem there is that you assume support for col names in csv. Unfortunately, because files are partitioned, it's not trivial to do that. Which partitions should  have col information? One, all of them? We can make up our own convention and support it, but csv is a transfer format from other tools. Unless we know what  other tools are going to do, it's pretty useless. As things are now, the solution is to remove headers from csv files and to provide that information at the format level, specifying col.names in make.input.format and also colClasses if you want to be absolutely safe (as class auto-detection may fail on very small partitions)

Please look into the vectorized.reduce argument to mapreduce. That requires you to also write a vectorized reducer, that is a reducer that can process multiple reduce groups in one call (in this case, multiple words). Writing an efficient one can be tricky. If I were doing this, I would form a data frame with keys and values than use dplyr to aggregate it (functions group and summarise).

Thanks for your private message providing a data sample. I can't respond privately, but here is what I found. First, your csv has a "," separator which is not default for csv in plyrmr, following the default of read.table. Second, your csv had a header row, which is not supported, so I removed it. After that, as far as I can tell, it works fine. Not sure that helps for your original dataset as it was in pig format, if I can remember.

temp.ag <http://temp.ag> <- input('~/Downloads/temp.ag.csv', format = make.input.format("csv", sep =","))
dcast(temp.ag <http://temp.ag>, formula = V1 + V2 ~ V3, value.var = 'V4')

On Monday, March 23, 2015 at 10:32:21 AM UTC-7, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:

> You are right! It's very similar to #26. What you specified as the input argument should be "format".
>
> input('/user/hive/warehouse/ag_temp', format = 'pig.hive')
>
> It's a problem with R generics, they force you to add the ... argument, then it doesn't catch simple mistakes like this. I could fix it with boilerplate code but it seems wrong. Once the format is not correctly set, the first time one needs to actually use the data (from.dfs or dcast, it doesn't matter) the wrong parser is used.

messages.body_plain:
I think you are using hdfs together with the local backend. Sorry if that's not made clear enough in the docs, but when using the local backend only local file system paths can be used. Only rmr2 and plyrmr are backend-aware, so that they switch from one file system to the other as one changes backend. rhdfs doesn't have a notion of swappable backend. It just works on hdfs. This could be what is making your program fail.

Antonio
